name: /reload on an installed binary restarts instead of failing the build
description: Job::Reload ran `cargo build --release` against MANIFEST_DIR = env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), the compile-time source path; on a release binary that is the GitHub Actions dir (D:\a\rusti\rusti), so /reload always failed with 'manifest path ... does not exist'. tui::reload_exe(manifest_dir, event_tx) now picks the binary to relaunch: with MANIFEST_DIR/Cargo.toml present it builds and stages exactly as before; without it, it posts a notice ('reload: no rusti source on this machine - restarting the installed rusti to reload config') and returns std::env::current_exe(). Both branches share build_relaunch_args and Event::Reload, so the session, model, url, key and flags carry over and config.json, models, themes and extensions are re-read.
evidence: cargo test (all pass): tui::tests::reload_without_source_relaunches_current_exe (non-existent manifest dir -> Some(current_exe), only the notice event, no cargo ToolStart or TaskEnd); relaunch_args_replace_model_and_dedupe_resume unchanged. Help text, /reload BUILTINS row, readme table and docs/tui.md updated.
decisions: Relaunching the running exe needs no staging: running an exe again is allowed while it is held, and Windows' thin-wrapper relaunch in run() already waits on the child.
No self-update: an installed /reload only restarts the same version.
